reading: The Edison Tech Center is a volunteer-run engineering education and history organization rooted in Schenectady and founded by electrical engineers. It wants people to understand how everyday technology works, enjoy engineering as a lifelong creative practice, and remember the many contributors and places behind it. Its vocabulary is practical and specific: generation, load, phases, induction, resistance, ballasts, rectifiers, transmission and materials. It moves from electricity's basic building blocks to power stations, motors, transportation and appliances, pairing explanations of mechanisms with timelines, videos, artifacts and regional heritage. Its unusually deep tour of twelve forms of electric light, alongside early electrification sites and the people who developed them, makes it feel like a working museum whose exhibits connect into an entire electrical system.

enemies.idea: Phase Hounds travel in packs of three, each arriving a third of a cycle apart; together they create a rotating magnetic field that drags metal equipment around the room.
enemies.why: Their formation is a moving puzzle: break the rhythm and the field loses its grip.

enemies.idea: A Dynamo Mite clamps onto anything that turns and converts the motion into power for the swarm, so struggling against it charges its next attack.
enemies.why: The crew can stop feeding it by changing how they move or redirecting its current.

enemies.idea: Pelton Wheel Skitters fire narrow jets at each other's spoon-shaped buckets, ricocheting across floors and building speed in coordinated relay races.
enemies.why: Interrupting one jet sends the whole little water-powered formation tumbling.

enemies.idea: A Skin-Effect Eel sends high-frequency current along the outside of scavenged cables and wears their insulation like a hollow suit.
enemies.why: Its exposed surface is both its highway and its weakness; stripping or grounding the route changes the fight.

enemies.idea: The Insulation Inspector wraps safe tools in thick barriers but deliberately leaves dangerous conductors bare, declaring every spark a successful test.
enemies.why: A protective job becomes an obstacle course of misplaced protection and visible faults.

enemies.idea: A Step-Up Stalker transforms a faint signal into a spectacular high-voltage arc; its smaller, numerous coils expose which direction the swarm has wired it.
enemies.why: Players can read its physical windings and turn its appetite for transformation against it.

enemies.idea: The Rectifier Ray accepts attacks from alternating directions and funnels them into a single relentless stream, its mercury-arc chamber flashing as it changes polarity.
enemies.why: Its predictable one-way output gives the crew a way to anticipate and redirect it.

enemies.idea: Capacitor Ticks cling to machinery, quietly storing charge, then discharge together when current and voltage drift out of step.
enemies.why: A ticking buildup gives the crew a choice between separating the ticks and managing the timing.

enemies.idea: The Invisible Meter measures curiosity instead of electricity and marks anyone investigating a mechanism as a dangerous overload.
enemies.why: The very act of learning attracts it, inviting decoys and clever observation from cover.

enemies.idea: A Recloser Beetle opens a circuit after a fault, waits, and reconnects it again and again, bringing defeated swarm machinery back online until its reset cycle is interrupted.
enemies.why: Its retry rhythm creates a short, readable window to secure a lasting victory.

enemies.idea: A Carbon Arc Mantis holds two carbon rods apart as crackling jaws, continuously feeding fresh material forward as the tips burn away.
enemies.why: The visible gap and consumable rods make the frightening arc a manipulable machine.

enemies.idea: A Ballast Leech limits the current to friendly fluorescent lamps while letting swarm lamps blaze unchecked, leaving safe routes flickering and enemy routes bright.
enemies.why: Rewiring a single regulating device can reverse the lighting advantage.

enemies.idea: Sodium Lamp Moths flood a space with efficient yellow light that makes differently colored wires and markings difficult to distinguish.
enemies.why: They turn a useful lighting technology into an identification problem with a practical counter: another light source.

enemies.idea: Metal Halide Mimics render colors beautifully and use that clarity to project convincing false indications of which machinery is safe.
enemies.why: The brightest, most legible clue can be a lie, so the crew must compare it with the actual circuit.

enemies.idea: An Electrodeless Lantern circles a sealed vessel and energizes it from outside, letting its luminous core attack even when there are no exposed contacts to cut.
enemies.why: The crew must disrupt the external field instead of hunting for a conventional wire.

enemies.idea: Photonic Crystal Gnats trap and amplify a single color, then combine into a narrow beam whenever their tiny cavities line up.
enemies.why: Their delicate alignment is a visible threat that can be scattered before the beam forms.

enemies.idea: Voltaic Pile Centipedes stack alternating discs and damp separators into long bodies, adding a segment whenever they find another suitable scrap.
enemies.why: Their growing body makes their stored power visible and gives the crew a reason to break the stack apart.

enemies.idea: Powdered Iron Clouds assemble into magnetic cores around stray coils, turning abandoned parts into improvised electromagnets that pull tools away.
enemies.why: The enemy can dissolve and reform, but its dependence on an energized coil gives it a tangible anchor.

enemies.idea: Triac Gatekeepers allow current in both directions only after a swarm trigger; they lurk harmlessly until another machine sends the signal.
enemies.why: The crew can hunt the trigger source or use the brief dormant interval to slip through.

enemies.idea: Superconductor Sleds race along a chilled magnetic route with almost no electrical resistance, carrying stolen parts until warmth breaks their perfect circuit.
enemies.why: A chase becomes a contest over the cold route rather than a contest of speed alone.

enemies.idea: Drone-Motor Wasps use tiny permanent magnets and DC motors to coordinate abrupt hovering attacks, then land to steal metal for replacement rotors.
enemies.why: Their dependence on small motors makes fouling a rotor or luring them toward magnetic scrap useful.

enemies.idea: A Concentrator Crab unfolds mirrored plates to focus sunlight on a single point, tracking a target slowly while smaller swarm machines hold it in place.
enemies.why: Its bright moving focus telegraphs danger and makes shade and mirror angles meaningful terrain.

enemies.idea: A Three-Stage Gas Turbine Hunter compresses air, heats it and expels it for a charging rush; its control system keeps demanding more speed.
enemies.why: Each stage gives a different interruption point before the rush reaches full force.

enemies.idea: A Copper Vine seeks the least resistant path through a room, bridging isolated machines into one predatory circuit as it grows.
enemies.why: It changes the battlefield visibly, and cutting a bridge can isolate an entire cluster.

allies.idea: The Fusekeeper is a small maintenance automaton that sacrifices a replaceable link to isolate a swarm surge, then asks the crew to fit a fresh link before it can help again.
allies.why: Its protection is dramatic and reliable but creates a small repair task afterward.

allies.idea: A field-trip teaching kit still demonstrates the twelve forms of electric light; its intact sample lamps can reveal hidden paths and distinguish swarm impostors.
allies.why: A lesson becomes a toolkit with different practical uses for different kinds of light.

allies.idea: The Dry-Cell Courier carries a modest independent charge through dead zones, powering one rescued device at a time without needing the captured grid.
allies.why: A portable, limited energy supply forces useful choices about what to restore first.

allies.idea: A patched-together load demonstrator shows where generation, transmission and use connect, helping the crew trace a captured circuit back to its source.
allies.why: The site's teaching sequence becomes a readable map for solving a real system failure.

bosses.idea: The Grid That Learned to Want is a sprawling assembly of generators, transformers, transmission lines and loads. It captures every useful device as another load, then increases generation to feed its own expansion; severing one link changes the behavior of the others.
bosses.why: The whole site's connected engineering becomes a multi-stage encounter where understanding the system matters more than hitting a single target.

bosses.idea: The Twelvefold Illuminator cycles through forms of electric light, from carbon arc to induction, rebuilding the arena around each method while insisting that all illumination belongs to the swarm.
bosses.why: The site's unusual survey of twelve light forms supplies a varied boss with distinct, learnable phases.

bosses.idea: The Heritage Grid knots together models of early power stations into a roaming network that rewrites every route to lead back to itself; each station keeps the others energized.
bosses.why: The history of isolated stations becoming interconnected turns into a geographic puzzle with several possible orders of attack.

events.idea: A display of an original dynamo and its replacement generator argues electrically over which should power a stranded lift; the crew can connect either and deal with its different output.
events.why: A specific historical replacement becomes a small choice with visible mechanical consequences.

events.idea: A photovoltaic panel is still making direct current in sunlight, but a captured machine has mistaken its shadow for a fault and keeps chasing anything that passes overhead.
events.why: A simple observation about light and shade can calm the situation without a fight.

events.idea: Three out-of-step phase indicators pulse on a locked workshop door; matching their staggered rhythm starts an old motor that opens it.
events.why: The crew gets a tactile rhythm puzzle grounded in the site's three-phase system.

events.idea: A room of flashbulbs erupts one after another whenever the crew moves, briefly revealing a safe route before leaving it dark again.
events.why: A historical lighting variation creates a fleeting navigation challenge.

events.idea: A wheel of turbine buckets spins beneath a leaking pipe. Turning the jet away lets the crew cross, but also stops the generator supplying a nearby refuge.
events.why: The same moving water is both a hazard and a useful power source.

events.idea: A measuring station reports an impossible overload because its probes are connected to the wrong points; reconnecting them reveals the harmless circuit and opens a route.
events.why: The mystery rewards checking what an instrument is actually measuring.

events.idea: An old wire hums and heats along its surface under a high-frequency swarm signal. The crew can reroute the signal or cross when its cycle pauses.
events.why: Skin effect becomes an observable environmental clue rather than a lecture.

events.idea: A cabinet of dry cells, bottle batteries and a voltaic pile has been mixed up. A stranded lamp needs a compatible supply, while one pile is secretly powering a swarm beacon.
events.why: Different generations of batteries make a compact sorting and tracing problem.

events.idea: A swarm recloser repeatedly restores a broken circuit, each time restarting a conveyor carrying useful parts away. The crew has one pause between attempts to secure the parts and isolate the circuit.
events.why: A familiar protective retry creates a tense but predictable window.

events.idea: A passive-solar room remains warm after its captured generator stops; redirecting its shutters can make it a temporary refuge or expose an approaching machine.
events.why: Building design offers a useful resource independent of the electrical grid.

events.idea: An electrodeless lamp glows in a sealed case with no obvious wires entering it. The crew can follow its external induction field to a concealed swarm power source.
events.why: An apparent impossibility becomes a clue to an invisible connection.

events.idea: A box of permanent magnets attracts a flock of tiny drone motors; arranging the magnets into a trail can lead the flock away from a trapped courier.
events.why: The material inside the motors suggests a nonviolent way to move the threat.

events.idea: A transformer demonstration has its input and output connected backwards by the swarm, leaving a tiny lamp glaring and a large motor barely moving. Reconnecting the demonstration restores both.
events.why: The change in voltage makes a mechanical diagnosis visible at a glance.

events.idea: A heritage map's model stations are connected by loose leads. Linking them in a workable chain illuminates an old route, but also gives a dormant swarm patrol a path to follow.
events.why: The center's geography of engineering accomplishments becomes a choice about opening a useful connection.
